process.title: What happens when you ask
process.intro: You can ask for yourself, for your child, or for someone you care about. Here is what happens after you reach out.

steps.name: Submit a request
steps.text: Tell us what you are living with and how it affects your daily life. You can add photos if you like.

steps.name: Initial review
steps.text: Our team reads every request and considers whether surgery could help and whether it fits what our ministry can do.

steps.name: Conversation
steps.text: If we may be able to help, we will contact you to learn more and answer your questions.

steps.name: Decision
steps.text: We consider each request prayerfully, weighing medical need against the resources we have.

steps.name: Care and support
steps.text: If we move forward together, we stay with you through surgery and recovery, and long after it ends.

process.assurance: You will never be pressured, and what you share stays confidential. You can ask us questions at any point.
process.draftNote: These steps are a draft from the ministry's founding notes and will be confirmed before launch.

items.text: Reconstruction after an accident or injury, to restore function and appearance.

items.name: Conditions present from birth
items.text: Surgery for differences a person was born with, to improve function and quality of life.

items.name: Scars and burns
items.text: Treatment for scarring or burn injuries that limit movement or change how you look.

items.name: Reconstruction after cancer
items.text: Restoring form after cancer surgery or related treatment.

items.name: Restorative care

paragraphs.text: Care is free or offered at a reduced cost you can manage. We talk through any cost with you before anything is decided.

items.text: A few clear photos of the area

paragraphs.text: What you send us is health information, and we protect it that way. Only the ministry’s care team reads requests and sees photos. We never sell your information, and we use your photos only to review your request.
There are no advertising or tracking tools on the pages where you ask for help.

items.a: Injuries from accidents, conditions present from birth, scars and burns, reconstruction after cancer, and other restorative needs. The ministry’s care is reconstructive and restorative, so we don’t offer cosmetic procedures. If you aren’t sure your need fits, ask anyway.

items.q: Do I need insurance, a referral or medical records?
items.a: No. If you have insurance, tell us, because it may help us plan your care. Records are optional, and the names of doctors you’ve seen help too.
Only if you’d like. We offer prayer to every patient, and saying no never affects your care.

items.q: Who decides whether I can receive care?
items.a: Our team considers each request prayerfully, weighing medical need, the resources we have, and what our volunteer surgeons are able to do. If you live outside the Charlotte and Fort Mill area, ask anyway.

items.q: How long until I hear back?
items.a: We let you know we’ve received your request, and we aim to reply within 10 business days.
We’ll tell you plainly, and where we can, we’ll point you toward other care.

items.q: Can I ask by phone, or in Spanish?
items.a: Yes to both. Call us and we’ll go through the request with you, in English or Spanish. A Spanish version of this site is on the way.

stories.title: Stories
stories.lede: Real stories will appear here, each one shared with the patient’s written permission. Until then, these samples show how a story will look.
stories.sampleLabel: Sample story, not a real patient

items.quote: I hadn’t worn short sleeves in eleven years. The summer after my last appointment, I wore them to church.
body: A kitchen fire left scars across her forearm and the inside of her elbow. Over the years the skin tightened until she couldn’t fully straighten her arm.
A friend from her Bible study sent us her name. After two surgeries to release the scar tissue, she has her full reach back. She still has scars, and she says she doesn’t mind them now.

items.quote: She used to cover her mouth in every photo. Now she’s the one asking to take them.
body: Their daughter was born with a cleft lip. It was repaired when she was a baby, but the repair left a scar that pulled at her lip as she grew, and the family’s insurance called a revision cosmetic.
The ministry’s surgeon revised the repair the summer before she started middle school, and the team checked in with the family all through her recovery.

items.quote: I thought I’d never hold a hammer again. Last month I helped frame a wall at my church.
body: A saw accident at work damaged two fingers and left his hand stiff and painful. He lost his job, and his insurance with it.
A social worker referred him to the ministry. Reconstructive surgery and months of hand therapy brought back most of his grip.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.lede: How Beauty From Ashes Surgical Ministry collects, uses and protects the information you share through this website.
privacy.draft: This notice is a draft. The ministry will publish its final privacy notice, including a HIPAA Notice of Privacy Practices, after legal review.

paragraphs.text: We collect what you choose to send through the forms on this site: requests for care, referrals, volunteer and partner forms, and messages. Requests and referrals can include health information and photos.
Like most websites, our host keeps basic server records, such as the date of a visit and the type of browser used.
We use your information to review requests for care, to contact you, and to coordinate volunteers and partners. We never sell your information, and we never use it for advertising.

Requests for care and referrals are protected health information under HIPAA. They are sent through a HIPAA-compliant service that has signed a Business Associate Agreement with the ministry, and only the ministry’s care team can see them.
This site uses no advertising or tracking cookies. Its fonts load from this site, so visiting does not report you to a font service.
If the ministry adds visitor statistics in the future, they will never run on the pages where you ask for help or refer someone.
You can ask to see, correct or delete the information you’ve sent us. Contact us by phone or email and we’ll respond within 30 days.
A parent or legal guardian sends requests for care for anyone under 18.
Questions about this notice? Contact the ministry by phone or email.

privacy.updated: Last updated: draft, not yet in effect.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.lede: Everyone should be able to learn about the ministry and ask for help, including people who use screen readers, keyboards, magnification or voice control.

paragraphs.text: We build and test this site against the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA. Accessibility is built into the site itself. We don’t use overlay widgets.

items.text: Every page works with a keyboard alone, with visible focus.
Form fields have labels, and errors say what to fix.
Forms have no time limits.
Text can be enlarged to 200%, and pages reflow at 400% zoom.
Animation stops when your device asks for reduced motion.
Pages work in high-contrast modes.

paragraphs.text: The Spanish translation is in progress, so some pages show English until it’s complete.
Sample stories and placeholder details on this demo will be replaced before launch.
Call or email us and we’ll help you another way, including taking a request for care over the phone. Please tell us what got in your way so we can fix it.
